worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ defined by $x=f(y,z)$ with $(y,z)\in D,$ the surface area of $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂x}{∂y})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂x}{∂z})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A.
$$

In this case, our surface is given by

$$
x={y}^{2}+\sqrt{3}z,\,(y,z)\in D,
$$

where 

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,0\le z\le y},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14066535/assets/0cf571155f2a4cd78d83c4808326cd8102badb3c22f43e00d95aee2494859f48.png)

Now, since

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2}+\sqrt{3}z)=2y, \\ \frac{∂x}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}({y}^{2}+\sqrt{3}z)=\sqrt{3},\end{aligned}
$$

the surface area is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂x}{∂y})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂x}{∂z})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+(2y)^{2}+(\sqrt{3})^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{4+4{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2\sqrt{1+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{y}\sqrt{1+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{1}\sqrt{1+{y}^{2}}\cdot z\,{|}_{z=0}^{z=y}\,\text{d}y \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{1}\sqrt{1+{y}^{2}}\cdot y\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting $u=1+{y}^{2},$ we get $\text{d}u=2y\,\text{d}y.$ Also, the limits must be changed as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & 0 & 1 \\ u & 1 & 2\end{aligned}
$$

 

Substituting these into our integral, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2{\int }_{0}^{1}\sqrt{1+{y}^{2}}\cdot y\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{u}^{1/2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{2}{3}{u}^{3/2}\,{|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}({2}^{3/2}-{1}^{3/2}) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}(2\sqrt{2}-1).\end{aligned}
$$
